title: Fix typos and unclear sentences in the Session 1 notes
body:
## Problem
The Session 1 notes may contain typos or sentences that a first-year student finds confusing.

## Context
Beginners judge the whole repo by Session 1.

## Expected outcome
A clearer `sessions/session-01/README.md` and `lesson.py` comments.

## Relevant files
`sessions/session-01/README.md`, `sessions/session-01/lesson.py`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] At least three improvements
- [ ] `python start.py test` still passes

## Difficulty
beginner

title: Add a colour-blind-safe palette to the Session 3 pressure arrows
body:
## Problem
The Session 3 app draws suction arrows in blue and pressure arrows in red; some colour-blind users cannot tell them apart, and the upper and lower Cp curves use the same pair.

## Context
Accessibility is part of the quality checklist (QUALITY.md, item 9).

## Expected outcome
A palette and line styles (for example dashed for the lower surface, arrow heads for suction) that stay distinguishable in light and dark mode.

## Relevant files
`sessions/session-03/app.html`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Suction and pressure distinguishable in grayscale
- [ ] Screenshot added to the pull request

## Difficulty
beginner

title: Add Session 4: a laminar boundary layer with Thwaites' method
body:
## Problem
The roadmap's first milestone does not exist yet.

## Context
See `promo/roadmap.md`, Session 4. The panel method gives the surface speed; the boundary layer needs it to grow.

## Expected outcome
`sessions/session-04/` with README (sections A to F), lesson, checkpoint, exercises and app in the same style as Sessions 1 to 3.

## Relevant files
`promo/roadmap.md`, `sessions/session-03/lesson.py`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Checkpoint prints PASS and the roadmap checkpoint (Blasius flat plate within 2 percent) is met
- [ ] Added to the tests

## Difficulty
intermediate

title: Add Session 5: transition and a turbulent boundary layer
body:
## Problem
Session 3 estimates drag with a fully turbulent flat-plate law that ignores the pressure; real airfoils keep some laminar flow and their drag depends on the pressure.

## Context
Roadmap Session 5.

## Expected outcome
A lesson and app where transition is found with Michel's criterion and the drag comes from the Squire-Young formula.

## Relevant files
`sessions/session-03/lesson.py`, `promo/roadmap.md`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] NACA 0012 at 0 degrees and Re = 6 million gives cd between 0.005 and 0.0065, shown in a figure
- [ ] Checkpoint added

## Difficulty
advanced

title: Reproduce the Target: an airfoil analyser with boundary layer, drag polar and stall
body:
## Problem
The Target couples the panel method to a boundary layer to predict the drag polar and stall; there is no public implementation.

## Context
The code behind the Target is private on purpose. The roadmap gives the path.

## Expected outcome
Your own implementation, written from the roadmap, plus figures like the Target for NACA 0012 and 2412.

## Relevant files
`promo/roadmap.md`, `promo/README.md`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] NACA 0012 at Re = 6 million: lift slope 0.10 to 0.11 per degree, minimum cd 0.005 to 0.0065, CL_max 1.3 to 1.7
- [ ] Short write-up of your method

## Difficulty
advanced

title: Show streamlines in the Session 3 live app
body:
## Problem
The Session 3 app shows pressure arrows and Cp but not the streamlines that the lesson figure draws.

## Context
Seeing the air curve round the nose and leave the trailing edge smoothly makes the Kutta condition visible.

## Expected outcome
A fourth graph button that traces a handful of streamlines with a simple Runge-Kutta step, using the panel strengths the app already computes.

## Relevant files
`sessions/session-03/app.html`, `sessions/session-03/lesson.py` (`velocity_field`)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Streamlines never enter the airfoil
- [ ] Runs smoothly on a phone
- [ ] Screenshot added to the pull request

## Difficulty
intermediate

title: Translate the Session 1 notes into Hindi
body:
## Problem
Students who prefer Hindi cannot read Session 1 comfortably.

## Context
This project teaches first- and second-year students across India; translations widen who can join.

## Expected outcome
`sessions/session-01/README.hi.md` with a faithful Hindi translation of sections A to F, linked from the main README.

## Relevant files
`sessions/session-01/README.md`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] All sections translated
- [ ] Equations, code blocks and file names unchanged
- [ ] Link added to the main README

## Difficulty
beginner
